questions.question: In digital circuit design, what does the "fan-out" of a logic gate specifically refer to?
options: The number of standard load inputs connected to and driven by the gate's output.
The maximum propagation delay measured across all internal transistor paths.
The ratio of dynamic power dissipation to static leakage power in the gate.
The physical layout area occupied by a cell relative to standard cell routing tracks.
The number of distinct clock domains a gate's output signal can simultaneously drive.

questions.question: In synchronous digital systems, what is the fundamental difference between clock skew and clock jitter?
options: Clock skew is the cycle-to-cycle variation in the clock period at a single point, while clock jitter is the spatial difference in arrival times between two registers.

Clock skew represents the spatial variation in clock edge arrival times across different locations, whereas clock jitter represents the temporal variation of clock edges over time at a given location.
Clock skew only affects hold timing constraints, whereas clock jitter exclusively impacts setup timing constraints.
Clock skew is caused solely by thermal noise in transistor channels, while clock jitter is caused exclusively by mismatched interconnect wire lengths.
Clock skew occurs only in dynamic logic styles, while clock jitter is restricted to static CMOS circuits.

questions.question: In modern microprocessor microarchitectures, what is the primary role of a dedicated Return Address Stack (RAS)?
options: To allocate stack frames in main memory for deeply nested recursive function calls.
To save general-purpose registers to on-chip SRAM during interrupt service routines.
To accurately predict the target addresses of subroutine return instructions (e.g., RET) in deeply pipelined execution.
To monitor hardware call stacks to detect and prevent buffer overflow exploits in software.
To store evicted dirty cache lines from the L1 instruction cache before writeback to L2.

questions.question: Why have advanced semiconductor manufacturing nodes (such as 3nm and below) transitioned from FinFET to Gate-All-Around (GAA) nanosheet transistor architectures?
options: To eliminate the need for chemical-mechanical planarization (CMP) in the middle-of-line (MOL) process.
To allow operation at significantly higher supply voltages (VDD > 1.8 V) for RF integration.
To replace copper interconnect layers with monolithic carbon nanotubes at lower metal layers.
To achieve superior electrostatic gate control over the channel, mitigating short-channel effects and reducing off-state leakage.
To reduce the total number of lithography masks required during extreme ultraviolet (EUV) exposure.

questions.question: In high-performance processor design, why is a Virtually Indexed, Physically Tagged (VIPT) scheme commonly selected for L1 data and instruction caches?
options: It completely prevents cache aliasing (synonyms) without requiring restrictions on cache line size, page size, or associativity.
It eliminates the need to verify physical address tags, thereby halving cache read power consumption.
It allows operating systems to manage cache replacement policies without maintaining physical page tables.
It avoids the need to invalidate cache lines when switching between distinct process address spaces.
It allows the cache index lookup and the TLB address translation to proceed in parallel, reducing L1 access latency.
